unit.title: Node.js: scripts and servers
unit.description: The Node runtime, ES modules and CommonJS, fs/promises, process.env and --env-file, the event loop, a minimal HTTP server, Express, built-in fetch

cards.definition: Two module systems. ES modules use import and export (the modern standard, "type": "module" in package.json). CommonJS uses require and module.exports (older Node code).
cards.example: import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises"; versus const fs = require("fs");

cards.definition: The Node module to read and write files with promises, so you can await them without blocking the server.
Configuration and secrets are read from environment variables in process.env, always as strings. Recent Node versions can load a .env file with node --env-file=.env, and .env is never committed.
cards.example: const key = process.env.STRIPE_KEY; if (!key) throw new Error("STRIPE_KEY missing");

cards.definition: Node runs your JavaScript on one thread. Slow operations (network, files) are handed off and their callbacks run later, so one server can handle thousands of connections. A long CPU loop, however, blocks everyone.
cards.example: A synchronous loop of 5 seconds in a request handler freezes every other request for 5 seconds.

cards.definition: The most common minimal web framework for Node: routes (app.get, app.post), middleware for parsing JSON, auth or logs, and responses with res.json. Fastify and Hono are faster modern alternatives.
Since Node 18, fetch exists in Node as in the browser, so calling an API from a script needs no extra package.
cards.example: const res = await fetch("https://api.example.com/stats"); const data = await res.json();

exercises.prompt: Why does document.querySelector fail in a Node script?
choices: Node has no DOM: there is no page to query
querySelector needs to be imported from npm first
The function was renamed in Node 22
exercises.explain: The DOM belongs to browsers. Node gives you files, network and processes instead.
import and export are the standard. require and module.exports are CommonJS, still found in older code.

exercises.prompt: This script runs with no MAX_LEADS variable set. What does it print?
exercises.explain: Environment variables are strings or undefined. ?? gives the fallback; convert with Number() if you need a number.

code.src:
const limit = process.env.MAX_LEADS ?? "50";
console.log(typeof limit, limit);

exercises.prompt: In which order are the lines printed?
exercises.explain: readFile is asynchronous: Node starts it, keeps running the code, and runs the callback when the file is ready.

exercises.prompt: A request handler runs a CPU-heavy loop for 3 seconds. What happens to other users?
choices: They all wait: the single JavaScript thread is busy
Nothing: each request has its own thread
The loop is moved to the browser
exercises.explain: Non-blocking I/O does not help with CPU work. Move heavy work to a worker thread, a queue or another service.

exercises.prompt: Where should the API key of your payment provider live?
choices: In an environment variable, never committed
In a constant at the top of server.js
In the README so the team can find it
exercises.explain: Secrets go in the environment (or a secrets manager). A .env file is fine locally if it is listed in .gitignore.

exercises.prompt: What does this Express route return to a GET /api/health request?
choices: An HTML page with the word ok
A 404, because routes need a database
exercises.explain: res.json serializes the object, sets Content-Type: application/json and sends status 200 by default.

exercises.prompt: Since Node 18, fetch can be used in Node without installing any package.
exercises.explain: True. The same fetch API as in the browser, handy for scripts that call APIs.

exercises.prompt: What does express.json() do in app.use(express.json())?
choices: Parses JSON request bodies into req.body
Converts every response to JSON text
Validates the JSON against a schema
exercises.explain: It is a middleware: it runs before your routes and fills req.body for requests sent as JSON.

exercises.prompt: How do you load a local .env file with recent Node, without a package?
choices: import ".env" at the top of the file
exercises.explain: Node 20.6 added --env-file. The dotenv package remains common in older projects.

exercises.prompt: This script must print the number of leads in leads.json. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explain: readFile from fs/promises returns a promise: without await, text is a Promise and JSON.parse fails. Write const text = await readFile(...).
